title: Stability Horizon: kernel oscillation containment and firebreaks
creator: Ava Chen
body:
Summary:
During a capacity rebalance on 2025-02-14 we observed repeated kernel-selection oscillations across a subset of inference workers which correlated with a sustained p95 increase (~2.3x) for conversational workloads. The behavior manifested as repeated re-selection between fused-attn and dequant fallback kernels inside a 30s window, causing microbatching churn, KV cache warm-up regression, and higher end-to-end latency.

Why this ticket exists:
This ticket captures containment actions already executed, proposed short-term mitigations, and a prioritized set of durable fixes (firebreaks) to prevent recurrence across bursty arrival patterns and scheduler probe windows. The goal is to land mitigations that are safe to ship as runtime-1.19 patches and follow with larger scheduler/kselection refactors in subsequent releases.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: p95 latency regressed for ~12% of active hosted API clusters for ~3 hours, impacting chat responsiveness for high-concurrency tenants.
- Internal: elevated error budgets for two mid-size tenants; Support SLO alerting triggered and Pager duty escalated.
- Symptoms: oscillating kernel selection, microbatching fragmentation, increased KV cache miss rate, and transient GPU kernel thrashing.

Timeline (condensed):
- 2025-02-14 02:03 UTC: Alerting on p95 jump; automated rollback guard did not trigger because avg latency remained within threshold.
- 02:10 UTC: Initial investigation shows repeated kernel swap logs on worker-137.
- 02:34 UTC: Team disabled speculative kernel probing in production as a containment step (runtime flag flip).
- 03:05 UTC: p95 trended down but oscillation persisted intermittently; canary traffic was moved to a stabilized model variant.
- 05:45 UTC: Full mitigation: adjusted probe window to 10s and enabled hysteresis on kernel-score deltas.

Root cause hypothesis (evidence-backed):
1) Scheduler probe window and our microbatch sampling introduced feedback where short bursts of arrivals caused the kernel scorer to flip affinity between fused-attn and a dequant-fallback path. The scorer used transient microbatch latency as a primary signal without smoothing.
2) KV cache warm-up penalties amplified the measured latency difference on the fallback path, making short-lived probes appear better or worse depending on exact traffic phase.
3) The runtime lacked a circuit-breaker/hysteresis layer around kernel re-selection decisions; small score deltas immediately caused recompile/selection churn.

What we did (containment and short-term mitigations):
- Disabled speculative probing globally for 3 hours while investigating (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1324).
- Applied an emergency probe-window reduction and 30s cooldown for kernel-score flips in canaries (release runtime-1.19.1).
- Re-routed a small percentage of heavy-chat tenants to a pinned model variant that uses only the stable fused-attn kernel to reduce customer impact.
- Updated alerting to include kernel-flip-rate metric so we can detect oscillation earlier.

Durable fixes (priority ordered):
1) Hysteresis + dampening layer for kernel-score deltas (owner: Diego Morales, ETA: 2025-03-12) — add exponential smoothing and require sustained advantage for N seconds before switching.
2) Circuit breaker for probe-induced recompiles (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2025-03-20) — cap recompile frequency per worker and open a temporary quarantine window if thrashing detected.
3) KV-warmup-aware scoring (owner: Marco Alvarez, ETA: 2025-04-01) — integrate a warmup penalty so early cold-cache samples do not dominate decisions.
4) Scheduler probe policy revamp (owner: Diego Morales + Scheduler SIG, ETA: 2025-Q2) — separate probe signals for throughput vs latency and introduce load-aware probe pacing.
5) Canary augmentation and gate framework (owner: SRE team; leads: Hannah Li, ETA: 2025-03-05) — add kernel-flip-rate and kv-miss-rate gates to our canary checklists.

Monitoring & observability additions (short-term):
- New dashboard: Kernel Stability Horizon (shows kernel-flip-rate, per-worker recompile-count, kv-cache-hit-trajectories, microbatch-size distribution).
- Alert: kernel-flip-rate > 5 per minute per worker for 3 consecutive minutes -> page on-call.
- Metric tagging: add request-level flag indicating 'probe-originated' to track probe impact on downstream metrics.

Rollback and safety plan:
- Runtime flags for speculative probing and scoring hysteresis are feature-gated; on regression we can flip the gate and re-evaluate.
- Canary rollout plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% with kernel-flip-rate and p95 SLO gate at each step.

Open action items (trackers):
- [A1] Implement hysteresis/dampening in scorer and unit tests (ENG-317642-A1) — Diego — in progress — target 2025-03-12.
- [A2] Add recompile rate limiter and worker quarantine (ENG-317642-A2) — Priya — todo — target 2025-03-20.
- [A3] KV warmup simulator and adjusted scoring weight experiments (ENG-317642-A3) — Marco — todo — target 2025-03-28.
- [A4] Dashboard + alerting changes (ENG-317642-A4) — SRE (Hannah) — in review — target 2025-03-03.
- [A5] Canary gate definitions and runbook update (ENG-317642-A5) — Diego/Hannah — todo — target 2025-03-05.

Related artifacts and links:
- Incident notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/12345678/2025-02-14+kernel+oscillation+incident
- Slack incident thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234ABCD/p1676361234000000
- Emergency PR (probe disable): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1324
- Canary rollout plan doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/canary/kernel-horizon-2025-02

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Hysteresis and recompile-rate limits merged and deployed to canaries with no p95 degradation on canary clusters.
- New dashboard and alerts firing on synthetic tests that oscillate kernels.
- Runbook updated with step-by-step rollback and quarantine instructions.
- Post-deploy 72-hour observation window with no kernel-flip-rate spikes above threshold.

Notes and recent updates:
- 2025-02-20: Diego pushed prototype hysteresis branch and captured synthetic replay showing 87% reduction in flip-rate under bursty workloads.
- 2025-02-24: SRE implemented kernel-flip-rate dashboard; early visibility shows several low-volume tenants had sub-threshold oscillations for the past month.
- 2025-03-03: We validated canary gating logic in staging; next step is production 1% rollout once PR review completes.

Slack mentions for escalation: @oncall-runtime, @sre, @pm-core.

If anything changes during implementation we'll add short updates as notes below and link to incremental PRs.
